content: Svasti Siddhaṃ!Though all the Munis are equal in their qualities of abandonment and realization,To the courageous heart of profound love for beings difficult to tame,The object of praise by all the Victors of the ten directions with one voice,To the Bhagavan Śākya Sengé, I bow my head in homage.Urged by the Sugatas, he bound the diadem upon the head of Ajita,And with the five observations, he looked upon the beings of Jambudvīpa;To guide them onto the authentic path, from Tuṣita,He descended—to the holy Tokar, I bow in homage.On the night of the fifteenth day of the waxing moon in the month of Saga Dawa,When the goddess Māyādevī was abiding in the purificatory fast,In the form of an ash-white elephant endowed with six tusks,To you who entered the womb, I bow in homage.On the tenth day of the month of Phālguna, when you were born from the right side,Wondrous and excellent signs appeared, and gods and nāgas offered service;By the power of the happiness of embodied beings, for whom you vowed this final birth,To you who bore the name Sarvārthasiddha, I bow in homage.In writing, swimming, taming elephants, and the like,Through mastery of the sixty-four arts,From your youth, you humbled the hosts of the powerful and arrogant;To you who stripped away their pride, I bow in homage.Until the age of twenty-nine, when you upheld the royal rule,To conform to the world and dispel all misconceptions,Taking as your queens those such as Sa-tsho and Grags-’dzin,To you who entered into marriage, I bow in homage.Urged by the melodious sounds of the Victor’s speech,And moved by the sight of aging, sickness, death, and a monk,You went forth into the religious life before the Immaculate Stūpa,To you who received the saffron robes from Indra, I bow in homage.At the Nairañjanā, in the space-pervading meditative absorption,When you practiced austerities for six years, through the power of the milkOffered as a restorative gift by Sujātā and others,To you in the prime of your golden-hued youth, I bow in homage.To attain supreme enlightenment in a single cross-legged posture,Upon the Vajrāsana, from the merchant Tashi,You took the bundle of Darbha grass and, having spread it,To you who remained steadfast in your vow of immobility, I bow in homage.When the demonic forces rained weapons and the beautiful ones tried to seduce you,You were not moved; as a witness to your countless offerings,When the Earth Goddess joined her palms, the gods of desireWith devotion offered you special praise; to you I bow in homage.Having reached the age of thirty-five,On the fifteenth day of the month of Saga, in the final of the six sessions,You filled the jewel of your mind with the essence of the nectarOf unsurpassed enlightenment; to you I bow in homage.After seven weeks, you spoke the auspicious verses,And urged by the Lord of the Celestials, in Vārāṇasī,On the fourth day of the month of Chu-stod, the four truths,The wheel of Dharma you turned; to you I bow in homage.Reaching the age of eighty, in the final month of spring,On the morning of the fifteenth day, the TathāgataAppeared to vanish from the realms of the world,And passed into nirvāṇa; to you I bow in homage.Though you taught for the sake of common disciples, to the body that has abandoned birth and death,The definitive meaning, I bow in homage.Opening wide the doors of the treasury of space,I present offerings, both actually arranged and mentally emanated, without end.All the negative actions and downfalls accumulated since beginningless time,I confess by means of the four remedial powers.In the virtues accomplished by myself and all others,I always rejoice with a heart of faith.I exhort you to turn the wheel of Dharma, which is not empty,For the sake of the Victors' heirs and their disciples until the end of cyclic existence.Without leaving all beings on the path to liberation,I pray that you remain firm and do not pass into nirvāṇa in your physical form.I dedicate the mass of merit thus accumulatedAs the cause for all beings to attain the wisdom of omniscience.May the fruits of this virtue throughout all the world systemsBe pervaded by great auspiciousness and well-being.This praise of the twelve deeds of our Teacher, the great and intimate friend of gods and men, the Kinsman of the Sun—composed at the request of Grong-smad-pa Sangs-rgyas-rgya-mtsho so that it might be easily understood by all, high and low, without being drawn out through poetic artifice or bound by obscure terminology and synonyms—was written by the Zahor monk Ngag-dbang-blo-bzang-rgya-mtsho at the Potala Palace on the second day of the waxing moon of the fifth month of the Fire-Snake year, with the scribe being the requester himself; Jayaṃtu.
